question: A 25-year-old sexually active male presents with an acutely swollen, hot right knee. Joint aspiration reveals turbid fluid with WBC 80,000/µL (>90% polymorphonuclear leucocytes) and no crystals. Which organism is the MOST likely cause in this age group?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! *N. gonorrhoeae* is the most common cause of septic arthritis in sexually active adults under 30. It may present as disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI) — migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, and dermatitis progressing to mono/oligoarthritis. Culture on Thayer-Martin (chocolate agar with antibiotics) in 5% CO₂.

Incorrect. *S. aureus* is the most common cause of septic arthritis OVERALL (especially in older adults, diabetics, prosthetic joints, and IV drug users). However, in a young sexually active adult, *N. gonorrhoeae* must be the first consideration.

Incorrect. *S. pneumoniae* is an uncommon cause of septic arthritis, seen occasionally in children or immunocompromised patients with pneumococcal bacteraemia — not a primary consideration in a young sexually active adult.

Incorrect. TB arthritis presents CHRONICALLY (weeks to months) as a 'cold' monoarthritis with insidious swelling — not an acute hot joint with 80,000 WBC. TB is granulomatous inflammation, not suppurative. Synovial fluid in TB shows lymphocyte predominance, not PMNs.

overallFeedback.feedback: Age-specific causes of septic arthritis: sexually active adults = *N. gonorrhoeae*; older adults/diabetics = *S. aureus*; children = *S. aureus* > *Kingella kingae*; prosthetic joints = coagulase-negative staphylococci. Joint WBC >50,000 with >75% PMNs = treat as septic until proven otherwise.

Septic arthritis in sexually active youth = think *N. gonorrhoeae* first. Cartilage destruction begins within 4–6 hours — aspiration and empiric antibiotics are emergency priorities. Remember: synovial membrane has no basement membrane barrier, allowing easy haematogenous seeding.
